Motivation
Under the Streams rebalance protocol, members send topology metadata when joining a group. The group coordinator compares this metadata with the topology already registered for the group to verify that the member uses the same topology. Each time a member joins or rejoins, the coordinator repeats structural comparisons of topology metadata that is typically identical across members. For Streams groups with large and complex topologies, these comparisons can impose a substantial workload on the coordinator. This workload can increase further when many members join concurrently, such as during application startup or rolling restarts.
Structural comparison also requires careful handling of representation differences that do not affect the topology’s meaning.KAFKA-21302demonstrated this problem: different orderings of equivalent copartition constraints could cause a valid member’s request to be rejected as an attempt to change the topology. Although that issue has been addressed, it illustrates the importance of explicit and consistent rules for determining topology equivalence.
This KIP proposes comparing standardized, client-computed topology hashes instead of repeatedly comparing complete topology structures on the coordinator. Clients can compute and cache the topology hash, reusing it as long as the topology remains unchanged. This distributes part of the computation required to establish topology equivalence across clients and reduces repeated structural comparison work concentrated on the coordinator. In particular, it can ease coordinator load when many members with large topologies join concurrently, contributing to more stable group management.
Defining a canonical representation and a deterministic hash algorithm ensures consistent hash computation across supported client implementations and versions. The complete topology will continue to be transmitted, allowing the coordinator to use it for group initialization and other operations that require topology information. The proposal aims to reduce repeated topology-comparison costs and coordinator load while preserving interoperability with clients and brokers that use the existing protocol.
